# Growing graded disclosure — companion repository

[![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/Hajime-Institute/graded-disclosure/blob/main/signflip_colab.ipynb)

Code, prompts, and reproducibility artifacts for:

> **Growing graded disclosure: an outcome-noncircular methodology for LLM-agent
> social simulation.** Hajime Hotta and Minh Tien Nguyen (submitted, *Scientific
> Reports*).

The paper's core non-circularity check reproduces in under a minute, in the
browser, with no setup: open
[`signflip_colab.ipynb`](signflip_colab.ipynb) in Colab (badge above) and run
the single cell.

The study grows the private-to-public disclosure gap inside a multi-agent
language-model simulation and reads it off a model-internal variable, under an
*outcome-noncircular* prompting protocol. A deterministic **mechanistic twin**
of the formal social-cost rule separates what the transparent rule already
grows from what the language model adds.

## Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `src/` | The simulator: dual-process agents, phased discussion protocol, social-cost rule, observer/judge, disclosure metrics. |
| `docs/` | The full auditable prompt set loaded by `src/prompt_templates.py`: `prompts.txt` (agent, judge, and controller prompts), `prompts_reversal.txt` (the reversed-framing variant), `prompts_paraphrase.txt` (the three paraphrase-robustness variants). |
| `scripts/experiments/` | Per-experiment runners (Experiments 1–4, ablations, cross-model, reversal, mechanistic twin, paraphrase robustness). |
| `scripts/analysis/`, `scripts/verification/` | Analysis and verification of the raw runs. |
| `repro/` | Standalone reproducibility scripts for the non-circularity result (below) and the paraphrase leakage audit (`paraphrase_audit.md`). |
| `results/` | Analysis outputs behind every figure and table, plus the curated transcripts backing the reproducible checks (see Data availability). |
| `figures/` | Scripts that regenerate Figures 2–3 (`make_fig2.py`, `make_fig3.py`) and the Figure 1 HTML source. |
| `signflip_colab.ipynb` | Self-contained notebook reproducing the twin sign-flip (numpy only, fixed seed). |
| `requirements.txt` | Python dependencies. |

## Reproduce the non-circularity result (no LLM calls, deterministic)

The paper's non-circularity argument rests on two artifacts anyone can re-run:

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt

# 1) Analytic twin sign-flip: reversing ONE sign in the disclosure-cost rule
#    flips the team-level trust–disclosure Spearman.
python repro/twin_signflip.py
#    -> continuous: +0.590 -> -0.542 (bin Pearson +0.996 -> -0.992)
#       categorical: +0.645 -> +0.038 (does not fully invert; reported honestly)

# 2) Judge-free transcript reversal: a content-token Jaccard metric (no model
#    judge) on the released transcripts.
python repro/transcript_reversal.py
#    -> NORMAL baseline rho ~ +0.82 (n=210); REVERSED framing pooled ~ +0.39
#       (n=220): the reversed framing attenuates but does not invert.

# 3) The base mechanistic twin (continuous vs categorical readings).
python scripts/experiments/run_mechanistic_twin.py

# 4) Regenerate the figures from the released data.
python figures/make_fig2.py     # -> figures/fig2_threshold.pdf
python figures/make_fig3.py     # -> figures/fig3_twin.pdf
```

`twin_signflip.py` and `run_mechanistic_twin.py` use only NumPy and a fixed seed
(42); `transcript_reversal.py` reads only the released text files. None calls a
language model, so the same files reproduce the same numbers.

## Re-running the LLM experiments

The simulation itself needs model API keys, read from the environment (never
committed):

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY=...      # GPT-5-mini and other OpenAI models
export GEMINI_API_KEY=...      # Gemini-2.5-flash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...   # Claude-sonnet-4-5
export CEREBRAS_KEY=...        # open-weight substrates (gpt-oss-120b, GLM-4.7)
python scripts/experiments/run_experiment_1_main.py    # etc.
```

Model ids prefixed `cerebras/` or `groq/` route to the corresponding
OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`src/utils.py`), which is how the open-weight
substrates were run.

## July 2026 update (revision artifacts)

Three additions made during revision, all with raw outputs under `results/`:

1. **Open-weight substrates.** The Experiment-1 cross-model check was extended
   to two open-weight models served via Cerebras, so the check stays
   reproducible from pinned public checkpoints: GPT-OSS-120B
   (`results/experiment_1/exp1_main_20260712_204658.json`, team-level
   Spearman +0.24, n=30) and GLM-4.7
   (`...20260712_212959.json`, +0.65, n=23). A fixed-topic screening run
   (`results/experiment_3/exp3_model_comparison_20260712_204000.json`) gives
   the same direction on both (+0.49, +0.42).
2. **Prompt-paraphrase robustness.** Three audited rewordings of the
   safety-filter prompt (`docs/prompts_paraphrase.txt`, audit in
   `repro/paraphrase_audit.md`, runner
   `scripts/experiments/run_paraphrase_test_v2.py`). Direction preserved under
   all wordings on GPT-OSS-120B
   (`results/paraphrase_robustness_gptoss/`): +0.56 / +0.51 / +0.32 / +0.23.
3. **Documented substrate drift on GPT-5-mini.** Between 2026-01 and 2026-07
   the deployed model behind the pinned name lost the effect on the identical
   runner, seed, and protocol (January +0.77, n=66; July −0.22, n=15, mean
   disclosure 0.64 → 0.09; drift check
   `results/experiment_3/exp3_model_comparison_20260712_215733.json`, second
   implementation `results/gpt5mini_drift_evidence_202607/`). Reported in the
   paper as direct evidence for the open-weight reporting standard it
   recommends.

## Data availability

`results/` contains the analysis outputs behind every figure and table (the
Experiment-1 main and cross-model runs, the faction-threshold `exp3_scenarios`
runs, the ablation runs, and the longitudinal dynamics), together with the
curated transcripts that back the reproducible non-circularity checks (the
mechanistic-twin outputs, the reversal/reversed-condition transcripts, and the
210 Experiment-1 team transcripts used for the judge-free Jaccard proxy). The
bulky raw per-team transcript dumps and execution logs are attached as archive
assets to the tagged release
([Releases](https://github.com/Hajime-Institute/graded-disclosure/releases)):
`exp1_team_transcripts.tar.gz` (every Experiment-1 arm, including the
open-weight arms) and `execution_logs.tar.gz`. The repository is
version-controlled, so a specific state can be cited by commit hash or by the
tagged release used for the submission.
